brooks_alignment.part_1_setup: Chapters 1-4 (~15,000 words, ~15%). Ben's restlessness and the wrongness in the Force. Luke's survey mission — both father and son feel the wrongness, but Ben's experiential pattern recognition (from years of exposure to the Force behaving wrong under Jacen, Abeloth, Vestara) leads him to interpret it differently. Ben considers and rejects a Jedi partner, calls Desh — a control choice disguised as a practical one (his Lie operating). Survey rhythm establishes Ben/Desh dynamic. Discovery of perimeter facility, seal warning, fortress coordinates. Arrival at the fortress: four-level vertical descent into a mountain — operations level, archive level, stasis ring (twelve chambers: nine dark with bodies, three active with living occupants, one empty and broken open from inside), and Gavran's central chamber where his body sits at the nexus of the anchor system. The fortress tells the story through environment before anyone explains it.
brooks_alignment.first_plot_point: Chapter 5 (~5,000 words). Single-shock FPP per D8. The survivors awaken — three humans, human register carrying the dramatic soul of the scene — and one institutional fact detonates: the Ruusan Reformations were dual-purpose (public reform + private penance). That is the FPP shock (R04a). Survivor introductions carry character distinctness per R8 (Sera's precision, Torin's warmth, Kael's dry corrections must emerge as persons before exposition density is permitted). The empty chamber is left as unresolved mystery. Technique, wound mechanics, anchor system, and Brotherhood inversion details are deferred to Ch 7 / 9 / 11 (R04b/c/d) to give each revelation dramatic air and to build institutional-question momentum feeding the Ch 21 SPP. Veraine is named at Ch 6 s1 (R05 moved from Ch 5 s3 per D8). Dual threat (seal failing AND someone already moving) lands by Ch 6; Ben's lock-in begins at Ch 5 and completes at Ch 6.
brooks_alignment.part_2_response: Chapters 6-12 (~26,250 words, ~26%). The group travels the Ruusan Corridor — now understood as the seal's infrastructure network connecting anchor nodes. Each stop is a failed or failing node with escalating severity: the Battlefield Node (mild thin place, minimal Veraine trace), the Brotherhood Outpost (moderate degradation with dark-side residue, heavy Veraine activity and deliberate message aimed at Kael), Maetha's Training Facility (psychologically intense, the Weave gone flexible, Maetha's warning delivered, Torin's rationalization begins). Transit chapters aboard the Steady Returns deliver the Ankhural Codex framework, the Ben/Desh Jacen conversation, and the Kael/Desh friendship. Veraine's trail reveals she's not just researching — she's repurposing each node into an amplification array, turning the seal's own infrastructure against itself.
brooks_alignment.midpoint: Chapter 13 (~4,500 words floor, may run shorter per D6). Experiential midpoint, not informational. Full breach experience — the group enters a node Veraine deliberately collapsed as a field test for her Veranthos ritual. Complete unweaving: the Force present but formless, every choice Ben's alone (the missing stop-signal), Desh's environmental wrongness crossing into undeniable. Per D7 Component A, Torin's response is unreadable — NOT a smile that closes the corruption arc at the midpoint. Per D6, Ben's reactive-to-proactive pivot is behavioral, not verbal: the unmade Luke check-in. He was scheduled to comms-back to Luke at departure from Kolven; he doesn't make the call. No declaration; the silence is the pivot. Per B1, an additional realization lands — Veraine's technique requires a specific geographical anchor, reframing Veranthos and rerouting the mission from Ch 14. Per B2, the cascade-acceleration principle is seeded subtly through the breach experience (Ben senses how things hold together or apart not by intention but by what bears weight). Naming what Veraine has been doing is split off the midpoint and lands in Ch 14 s1 as response-quadrant processing (D6 Fix 1).
brooks_alignment.part_3_attack: Chapters 14-20 (~26,250 words, ~26%). Ben takes command — the Ch 13 behavioral pivot extends into Ch 14 where Ben already holds the B1 amplification-array-dependency fact and reroutes the mission on that basis. Ch 14 s1 absorbs the naming of what Veraine has been doing (D6 Fix 1). Sera's conditional trust ('Tell me where to stand, Skywalker') reinforces her Lie — she's following someone again without examining the pattern (Ch 14). Gavran's resonance note planted. Veraine's truce meeting (Chapter 16): three-objective operation per W2 — ideological pitch, Kael recruitment, intelligence gathering (as Ben's attention rather than scripted beat). Sabotage is NOT an in-meeting objective; Veraine's crew executes sabotage in a separate scene distributed across Ch 16 exit and Ch 17 opening. Sera counters with firsthand testimony. Chapter 17 triple-register absorption: sabotage discovery opens the chapter; Sera-stops-defending-Torin lands (D7 relocation, triggered by Kael's direct question per W1 Inversion 2); Kael's question is also the W1 beat. Three quiet threads, thematically related. Chapter 18: sabotage consequence reverberates; Sera's lie_fissure lands (B1 Part 2 — first visible doubt about 'principle alone is enough', brief/unspoken, also first intuition of cascade-acceleration behavior); Ben recognizes the Jacen pattern in Torin and names it explicitly (the R13 single-explicit-naming budget); the loudest visible Torin-telegraph beat lands concurrent with the Jacen naming. The Jedi outpost (Chapter 19): modern Knights experiencing Weave distortion — grounds cosmic stakes in present suffering, Torin weaponizes their pain as argument, Sera's moment of truth as she sees principled certainty isn't protection. Kael articulates the single-framework critique (his moment of truth). The Jacen parallel now operates subtextually. Arrival at Veranthos (Chapter 20): the ring structure of escalating wrongness, Veraine already at the wound source; conditional W2 Option α slot for a Veraine near-miss or failed-interception beat, or a ledger entry if α is dropped.
brooks_alignment.second_plot_point: Chapter 21 (~4,500 words). Torin's turn. 'I am not asking for permission.' He leaves to become the new seal — repeating Gavran's pattern of noble self-sacrifice. Per B2, the group's non-interdiction is dual-ballasted: the articulated thematic refusal carries the book's line ('I was the one they sealed. I cannot seal another.') and is the ONE thing spoken aloud; the tactical refusal registers silently — cascade-acceleration (forcible disengagement of an entangled Force presence would rip the seal faster than Torin's unchecked arrival) and Torin's counter-preparation (a dead-man's trigger on his own Force presence, anticipating the interdiction options). Sera reads the counter-preparation in the Weave (her lock-sense expertise is the diagnostic instrument); Ben registers the cascade-acceleration through Sera and Desh's combined reads. No one gives a speech. Each character's additional arc-rooted texture remains: Ben (failed to stop Jacen, has no alternative yet), Sera (was the person whose agency was overridden — cannot do to Torin what Gavran did to her), Kael (spent his life being stopped and redirected — won't do it to someone else), Desh (breaks silence with operational pragmatism). Ben's crystallizing realization: 'We find another way. Together.' The Lie cracks open. Per R13, the Jacen parallel is not re-articulated here; it operates subtextually.
brooks_alignment.part_4_resolution: Chapters 22-28 (~28,000 words, ~28%). Ben and Sera find the resonance solution (Chapter 22). Kael commits freely — 'If this kills me, I want it on record that I volunteered. First time for everything.' (Chapter 23). Three-way convergence at the Scar: Veraine at the epicenter performing her amplified ritual, Torin descending the ridgeline deploying the technique, resonance trio at mid-valley, Desh off-site sabotaging amplification nodes against Veraine's crew guards. Resonance starts discordant, catches when Ben stops trying to control it. Two-stage defeat of Veraine: Desh removes amplification, resonance produces emergent complexity she can't model. Torin's technique works but consumes him — pulled free by Sera, alive but diminished. New seal: dynamic, harmonic, requiring periodic renewal. Denouement: Veraine contained not killed, Torin diminished (Sera stays), Kael departs freely, Desh and Ben laugh. Chapter 28: Ben tells Luke everything. The Order will know the truth.
brooks_alignment.inciting_incident: Chapter 1. Luke's survey assignment lands on Ben's datapad while Ben is still processing the sparring failure. The wrongness stops being ambient and becomes institutional — Ben now has cover and coordinates to pursue it. The disturbance has found him; the story has begun.
brooks_alignment.first_pinch_point: Chapters 10-11. The Brotherhood Outpost. Veraine's trail goes hot: she has been through the facility days ahead of the group, extracted the research infrastructure, and left a deliberate message aimed at Kael. The reader sees the antagonist's active hand for the first time. Veraine escalates from absent presence to operational threat without the plot skeleton advancing.
brooks_alignment.second_pinch_point: Chapter 18. The seal sabotage hits. Veraine has used the truce meeting to deliver targeted damage and the timeline collapses from weeks to days. Ben names the Jacen pattern in Torin out loud to Desh. The antagonist force presses and the internal antagonist reveals he is locked onto a course. Every pressure dial is red; the attack phase is failing.
brooks_alignment.climax: Chapters 25-26. The three-way convergence at the Scar. Veraine's amplified ritual, Torin's unilateral technique deployment, Desh's off-site sabotage of the amplification array, and the resonance trio (Ben, Sera, Kael) at mid-valley. Per B3, Ben's resonance-enhanced Force-sense reads the containment nodes as load-bearing points in the Weave (not Desh himself); targeted comm-bursts carry tactical facts that require language; the heartbeat beat (node wobble + Desh re-stabilisation call) renders a single high-tension moment by alternating channels. Per D2 Ch 25 s3, Ben holds the interpretive axis of the resonance — composing Sera's lock-sense, Kael's unintegrable signature, and Desh's operational frame into one executable chord. Two-stage Veraine defeat: Desh removes amplification, resonance produces unmodellable emergent complexity. Torin's technique works but consumes him. New seal stabilizes dynamic and harmonic. Per D2 Ch 26 s3, Ben takes the first share of the new seal's ongoing ethical load on himself — becomes the first anchor. Per R13 rule 12, the Jacen parallel remains subtextual throughout the climax.

Relationship turns register implicitly through proximity, speech order, texture of silence rather than through scripted dialogue beats. Ch 13 may run shorter than 4,500 words — allowed.
structural_notes.voice_architecture_cm4: Per CM4: the book runs on a five-anchor voice architecture (Zahn primary ~60-65% / Luceno payload ~20-25% / Allston ensemble architecture / Stover constrained ~5% / Bujold interior ~15-20%). Scene-type → anchor mapping is codified in voice_definition.scene_type_anchor_mapping. Anti-slop rules restructured into a two-tier set: 17 derived_rules (CM4 + FG2b + R11 + R13 + D3 + D4 + D7 + W1 + W2 + B3) governing what kind of book this is; 25 line_level_rules preserving granular prose-craft guardrails. The spec is NOT 'airport bookstore / commercial tie-in' — that framing has been retired. Target audience is EU-literate Legends readers; primary comps Darth Plagueis / Outbound Flight / Memory. See top-level positioning_statement and comp_block fields.
structural_notes.hooks_convolution_notes: Per CM3: H06's 16-chapter lifespan is accepted as-is; D7's telegraph restructure (counter-currents at Ch 8/11/15/18, Sera-stops-defending moved to Ch 17, loudest telegraph to Ch 17-18) makes the long lifespan live through authentic ambiguity rather than slow confirmation. relationship_arcs.want: To be father and son without the Order between them.
relationship_arcs.need: To choose the private relationship actively, not wait for circumstances to permit it.

voice_definition.pov_approach: close third-person limited, locked to Ben Skywalker throughout
voice_definition.prose_register: Adult Legends fiction. Luceno-density payload inside Zahn-clarity prose, with Bujold-warmth interior carrying Ben's close-third. The surface reads clean, propulsive, and transparent (Zahn); the density lives in what each scene is *about*, not in how it reads (Luceno); Ben's interior register carries self-aware character-warmth adjacent to Bujold's Miles Vorkosigan — capable of self-deprecation, aware of its own patterns, hurt-without-performance. This is NOT airport-bookstore commercial tie-in; it is NOT literary-fiction experimentation. It is a dense-content Legends novel whose sentences do not call attention to themselves. Payload chapters (Ch 5, 7, 9, 11, 12, 16, 28 s2) lean into Luceno-technique for lore delivery; Force-interior peaks (Ch 13, 25, 26) unlock a constrained Stover budget. Elsewhere, Zahn-clear baseline with Bujold interior texture.

reference_authors.author: Timothy Zahn
reference_authors.scene_defaults: Close-third baseline, investigation, transit, action, most dialogue scenes, all chapter connective tissue
reference_authors.benchmark_works: Heir to the Empire, Thrawn Trilogy; Outbound Flight (co-signal with Luceno); Specter of the Past (register anchor, not tonal comp)
reference_authors.what_to_emulate: Clean, precise, efficient prose. Dialogue that advances plot and reveals character simultaneously. Intelligent characters who sound intelligent without lecturing. Sentences that do their work and get out of the way. Short paragraphs. Action scenes with tactical clarity. When in doubt about prose choices, ask 'would this sentence appear in a Zahn novel?' — if it is ornate or introspective beyond a line or two, the answer is no.
reference_authors.what_to_avoid: Zahn's prose can run emotionally cool — functional rather than felt. This book covers that gap with the Bujold interior register (see below). Do not mimic Zahn's cool by suppressing Ben's warmth; the combined register is Zahn-clear sentences carrying Bujold-warm interior. Also: do not import Specter-era political-thriller framing; this is not that kind of book (see comp_block.anti_comps).

reference_authors.author: James Luceno
reference_authors.scene_defaults: Payload chapters Ch 5 / 7 / 9 / 11 / 12 / 16 / 28 s2; technique-lineage exposition; archive-processing scenes; institutional-complicity argumentation
reference_authors.benchmark_works: Darth Plagueis (primary comp); Tarkin; Outbound Flight
reference_authors.what_to_emulate: Lore integration that feels organic rather than encyclopedic. Luceno weaves EU history into narrative without stopping for footnotes — information lands through character reaction (shock, recognition, reassessment, memory), never as free-standing narrator exposition. This is a *technique*, not a prose register: Luceno payload goes inside Zahn-clear sentences.
reference_authors.what_to_avoid: Luceno's sentence-level pacing can run slow and dense; do NOT adopt Luceno's sentence length or paragraph shape. Borrow only the exposition-through-reaction technique. If a paragraph reads slow, it has absorbed the wrong thing from Luceno.

reference_authors.author: Aaron Allston
reference_authors.weight: Active whenever three or more speakers share a scene
reference_authors.scene_defaults: Group scenes on the Steady Returns, Ch 5 survivor waking, Corridor-stop deliberations, Ch 19 outpost, Ch 24 array setup, all multi-speaker deliberation beats
reference_authors.benchmark_works: Wraith Squadron; X-Wing: Starfighters of Adumar (register anchor ONLY — tonal anti-comp, see comp_block)
reference_authors.what_to_emulate: Voice-distinction discipline: each named speaker identifiable by register within two exchanges without attribution tags. Scenes that move — no scene overstays its welcome. Rhythmic cross-talk that distributes story-work across speakers rather than routing everything through one mouth.
reference_authors.what_to_avoid: Allston's flippant caper-register is WRONG for this book. Humor present (per humor_register) but never deflating. The Torin turn, the breach experience, and the climax are humor-free zones. Borrow Allston's ensemble-architecture ONLY; do not borrow Starfighters-era comedic tone.

reference_authors.author: Matthew Stover
reference_authors.scene_defaults: Ch 13 breach (extended allowance); Ch 25 void/resonance (extended allowance); Ch 26 living seal (extended allowance). Elsewhere: maximum one Stover-permitted interior beat per chapter, flagged in scene cards as `stover_permitted: true`.
reference_authors.benchmark_works: Traitor (NJO) — Force-philosophical interior under theological pressure; Shatterpoint — Force-metaphysical register when earned
reference_authors.what_to_emulate: Interior intensity that renders Force phenomena through a body that is *inside* the perception, not analysing it. Reserved for moments whose payload the reader has earned through preceding accumulation.
reference_authors.what_to_avoid: Stover's purple prose, extended introspective passages outside the allowance windows, sentence-fragment stylistic tic as a general voice. A chapter outside Ch 13 / 25 / 26 that reads like Stover's general voice is a chapter that needs to be rewritten toward Zahn. Sentence fragments as a stylistic pattern (rather than a rare emphasis beat) are out of register.

reference_authors.author: Lois McMaster Bujold
reference_authors.weight: ~15-20% of Ben's close-third interior texture; distributed throughout
reference_authors.scene_defaults: Ben alone, Ben alone post-failure, Ben reading the room in ensemble scenes (paired with Allston for the exchange itself), two-person quiet conversations with Desh or Luke, Part 4 relational warmth
reference_authors.benchmark_works: Memory (closest overall non-SW comp); A Civil Campaign; Mirror Dance
reference_authors.what_to_emulate: Miles-Vorkosigan-adjacent interior: self-awareness without self-pity, warmth toward ensemble without sentimentality, personal-stakes political payload without lecture. Characters capable of noticing their own patterns and being hurt by them without performing the hurt. Humor from interior observation rather than from external wit. Political and institutional content carried through felt personal stake, not through authorial argument.
reference_authors.what_to_avoid: Bujold can spend extended pages in conversational banter or family warmth; the budget here is tighter. Borrow the interior register and the warmth calibration, not the page-space allocation. Do not import Barrayaran-political-specifics framing; borrow the *texture* of how political payload lives inside personal feeling.

scene_type_anchor_mapping.description: Each scene type has a primary anchor and one or two supporting anchors. Primary sets the prose surface; supporting anchors inform specific beats within the scene (interior texture, ensemble rhythm, payload-delivery technique, Force-interior register). Scene cards should flag the primary_anchor and supporting_anchor(s) per scene.

mappings.scene_type: Force-interior high-stakes (Ch 13 / 25 / 26 extended; elsewhere one permitted beat)

humor_register.calibration: Lightly humorous, Allston-tempered, Bujold-calibrated. Humor is texture present throughout the book, not a deflation device. It runs alongside serious content without undercutting it.

sources.Kael Drenn: Dry corrections and monk's-brevity observations — humor from understatement and after-the-beat timing
sources.Desh Rolan: Operational deadpan — the Allston channel — humor from pragmatic flatness against Force-user seriousness
sources.Sera Varik: Wryness — occasional, delivered straight; humor from precision rather than performance
sources.Ben Skywalker: Bujold-interior self-deprecation — Miles-Vorkosigan-adjacent; capable of being funny in his own head about his own patterns
sources.Torin Hal (Ch 5-12): Narrative warmth that is genuinely funny in the way a gifted storyteller is funny — this is load-bearing for the corruption arc; when the humor thins in later chapters, the loss is felt
sources.Luke Skywalker: Sparing warmth that holds sadness — humor at the register of someone who has lost a great deal and still chooses to be present

humor_register.distribution: Early and middle chapters carry tempered humor as ensemble texture. Ch 13 (breach), Ch 21 (SPP), Ch 25 (climax interior), Ch 26 (climax resolution) are humor-free zones — the stakes require it. Ch 27 (quiet-after-climax) carries the book's most visible humor — the laugh-between-equals beat — earned by the weight of the preceding 26 chapters.
humor_register.anti_pattern: Humor never deflates a serious moment. Humor never flippantly engages stakes. No character quips during a genuinely escalating beat to lower tension. If a humorous line would cause the reader to disengage from the stakes, it is wrong for the scene regardless of how funny it is in isolation. The Allston reference is for architecture and distinction, NOT for Starfighters-era comedic deflation.

character_voices.Ben Skywalker:
Internal voice is sharp, self-aware, occasionally self-deprecating. Thinks in tactical assessments but feels in emotional undercurrents he doesn't always acknowledge. His humor is dry and defensive — he jokes to create distance. His narrative voice matures subtly across the book: more guarded and controlled in Part 1, more open and uncertain in Parts 2-3, more grounded and decisive in Part 4. He does NOT sound like Luke — he's more pragmatic, more skeptical, more his mother's son.

CRITICAL TRAP TO AVOID — the diagnostic voice: Ben is perceptive and tired. He should not also be the book's analyst, diagnosing the Force and himself with clinical vocabulary while events are happening around him. Early chapters must privilege reactive, tactile interiority — what his body does before his mind catches up, the thing he notices and can't name, the sentence he starts and cuts off. Conceptual compression (the 'structural, not emotional' framing of the Force disturbance, the 'both forms of Skywalker trap' self-analysis) is a Part 3-4 voice, earned by experience. In Parts 1-2 let him feel the problem before he can articulate it. If a sentence of Ben's interiority could be lifted into a mission debrief, it is too composed for the scene.

Specimens:
- "Desh. I need you for a survey run." / "How bad?" / "I do not know yet. That is the problem."
- He didn't reach for the Force. Not yet. The Force was the problem.
- "Fine. Keep your secrets. I will find them anyway."
character_voices.Sera Varik:
Dialogue is formal, archaic in syntax — no contractions early in the story, gradually loosening as she adapts. She speaks with precision and weight. Short sentences under pressure. Longer, more considered sentences in debate. She does NOT monologue — when she has something to say, she says it once and expects it to land. Her formality should soften specifically with Ben as trust builds — the shift from 'Skywalker' to 'Ben' is a marker the reader should feel.

Specimens:
- "Skywalker. The seal held for a thousand years because thirteen of us were the seal. Do not lecture me on containment."
- "I have fought beside people I did not trust. I have died with them. Trust and competence are separate questions."
- She touched the cut at her temple, considered it, and said nothing.
character_voices.Torin Hal:
Warm, easy, disarming. He tells stories. He uses humor to put people at ease. His dialogue should feel like the most *likeable* person in the room — which is what makes his turn devastating. As the story progresses, his warmth thins. The humor becomes slightly mechanical. The ease becomes slightly performed. The shift should be subtle enough that the reader feels it before they can name it. Post-technique in the climax, his voice flattens — still articulate but emotionally hollow.

Specimens:
- "You know what I love about modern Jedi? You still believe the dark side is a place you can choose not to go."
- "I sealed myself because I knew what I was becoming. Stasis was supposed to hold it. It did not."
- He smiled. He was always smiling by the end. It was one of the things that frightened Ben most.
character_voices.Kael Drenn:
Clipped, observational, dry. He doesn't volunteer — he responds. His humor is deadpan and often arrives after a beat of silence, as if he considered not saying anything and then couldn't resist. He speaks less than anyone else in the group. When he does speak, it tends to be the thing nobody wanted to hear. His voice should warm incrementally — not dramatically, just enough that the reader notices he's using more words per sentence by Part 4 than he did in Part 1.

Specimens:
- "Is this the part where I pick a side?" / "No." / "Good. I have not decided which one is lying yet."
- "Conviction costs more than anyone tells you when they are conscripting you."
- He did not volunteer. He waited, the way he always waited, until the room forgot he was there.
character_voices.Darth Veraine:
Precise, academic, unruffled. She speaks in complete, grammatically sophisticated sentences. No contractions ever. She asks questions she already knows the answers to. Her dialogue should feel like a university lecturer who happens to be discussing the fate of the galaxy. She is never sarcastic — sarcasm implies emotional investment. She is occasionally *curious*, which is more unsettling.

Specimens:
- "Consider what you have been taught to fear, Skywalker. Then consider who benefited from teaching it to you."
- "I am not interested in whether the wound hurts. Hurt is a small argument. I am interested in whether it is true."
- "You have two options. You may listen, or you may refuse to listen. Your decision does not alter the threadwork."
character_voices.Desh Rolan:
Casual, practical, professionally understated. Ex-intelligence operative who defaults to dry humor under stress. He speaks in shorter sentences than the Force-users because he's thinking about concrete things while they're debating philosophy. His humor is the Allston channel — grounding, well-timed, never at the expense of the moment's weight. He's the character most likely to say something the reader is thinking.

Specimens:
- "You are quiet." / "Mm." / "That is the bad kind of quiet." / "Yeah."
- "I used to carry a badge that said I was the law. Now I carry a charter that says I am insured. I prefer the charter."
- He checked the loading, checked it again, and then did the thing he always did before a firefight — cracked his neck and said nothing.
character_voices.Luke Skywalker:
Warmth holding sadness. Luke's voice has the specific quality of a Master who does not need his authority present in the room — the weight comes from the relationship, not from the title. Speaks in short sentences by preference; Grand-Master register surfaces only when the institution requires it, and never to Ben in private. He asks rather than tells. When he lands a hard thing, he lands it quietly — four words after a long silence, not a speech. His Force presence reads as vast, steady, and warm in a way that does not perform warmth. Post-Mara, post-Jacen, post-Abeloth: he carries the grief of a man who has lost more than most people will ever have, without any of it visible in his speaking voice.

Specimens:
- "And you didn't call me." (Ch 28 — four words that name the pattern without accusation.)
- "We'll tell the Council. All of it." (Ch 28 — decision rendered as we, not I.)
- His hands stayed on the desk through the entirety of Ben's telling. He did not need to move them.

Anti-pattern: Luke does not lecture. He does not invoke 'the Force' as an explanatory frame when speaking to Ben (they share the vocabulary; he does not need to cite it). He does not sigh, shake his head, or perform weariness — the weight is in the silences, not in the theatre. He does not deliver wisdom-dialogue of the 'you must learn that...' variety; if a line could appear in a Jedi Council scene, it is wrong for a Ben/Luke office scene.

anti_slop_rules.description: Two-tier rule set. Tier 1 (derived_rules) encodes the five-anchor architecture from CM4/FG2b/R11/R13/D4/D7/W1/W2/B3 and governs what kind of book this is. Tier 2 (line_level_rules) preserves granular prose-craft guardrails against AI-typical tics and generic patterns. Both tiers apply to every scene.

derived_rules.name: Sentence clarity always (Zahn)
derived_rules.content: Short-to-medium sentences; one idea per sentence; complex ideas built across sentences rather than crammed into one. No reader re-reading required except during explicit Stover-permitted passages (Ch 13 / 25 / 26 extended allowances; one permitted beat per other chapter). If a sentence makes the reader pause to parse it, it is wrong unless it is inside a Stover beat.

derived_rules.name: Exposition through reaction (Luceno)
derived_rules.content: New information lands through character reaction — shock, recognition, reassessment, memory, body-register. No free-standing narrator exposition. Archive material, technique lineage, institutional history all filtered through whose consciousness is registering the content and what it costs them to register it.

derived_rules.name: POV discipline absolute (Zahn)
derived_rules.content: Single close-third locked to Ben throughout. Other-character interiority rendered only through Ben's observation of behavior, speech, silence, micro-expression. No head-hopping. No narrator-omniscient slippage. If a sentence contains information Ben could not plausibly perceive in real time, it does not belong on the page.

derived_rules.name: Ensemble voice distinction (Allston)
derived_rules.content: Each named speaker identifiable by register within two exchanges without attribution tags. Signatures held across the book: Sera (precision — archival exactness, clipped clarity, century-of-discipline composure), Torin (narrative warmth rendered through Ben's misperception per D7), Kael (dry corrections, monk's brevity, understated pushback), Desh (operational flat, Allston-channel deadpan), Ben (Bujold-interior close-third, self-aware thinking-aloud), Luke (warmth holding sadness), Veraine (precise-without-affect, Socratic-adjacent questions-from-certainty per R14/W2). Voice drift between chapters is a drafting failure.

derived_rules.name: Stover budget (constrained)
derived_rules.content: One Stover-permitted interior beat per chapter maximum outside Ch 13 / 25 / 26 (extended allowances there). Scene-card marker: `stover_permitted: true`. Stover beats are reserved for Force-interior moments whose payload the preceding text has earned. Outside the allowance, Stover-register sentences indicate the scene needs to be rewritten toward Zahn.

derived_rules.name: Lightly humorous, Allston-tempered, Bujold-calibrated
derived_rules.content: Humor present as texture throughout (Kael's dry corrections, Desh's operational deadpan, Sera's wryness, Ben's Bujold-interior self-deprecation). Humor runs alongside serious moments, never deflates them. Bujold's Miles-Vorkosigan calibration: genuinely funny in interior voice, never flippant about stakes. Ch 27 carries the book's most visible humor, earned by Ch 1-26 weight; earlier chapters stay tempered. Ch 13 / 21 / 25 / 26 are humor-free zones.

derived_rules.name: Density lives in information, never in prose
derived_rules.content: Luceno payload encoded in what a paragraph is *about*, not in how it *reads*. Dense-content paragraphs still have Zahn-clear sentences. If a paragraph reads slow, it is carrying Luceno's sentence-level pacing by mistake; rewrite keeping the informational density inside faster sentences.

derived_rules.name: Concept-vs-sensation rule (D4)
derived_rules.content: POV and dialogue describe Force phenomena through what a body experiences (pressure, absence, lag, misread, missing handrail, architecture-slack, chrono-drift), not through analytical categories (residue, emergent, seductive, moral-intuition-suppressed). Analytical terms permitted only in (a) Veraine's ledger entries, which are explicitly flagged institutional-register, and (b) Gavran's archived notes, where the clinical voice is a character choice signalling his detachment. Elsewhere, concept-language is a violation. See force_mechanics.sensory_vocabulary for character-differentiated sensations.

derived_rules.name: Bujold interior register (Ben)
derived_rules.content: Ben's close-third carries Miles-Vorkosigan-adjacent self-awareness — capable of self-deprecation, aware of his own patterns, hurt-without-performance. Applied especially post-failure and in ensemble-regard moments. Paired with Allston during ensemble dialogue: Bujold for Ben's internal reading of the room, Allston for the exchange itself. This is the warmth that offsets Zahn's cool prose surface.

derived_rules.name: Render the Weave argument; never declare it (FG2b)
derived_rules.content: The Weave-as-imposed-structure theological claim is rendered through events and consequences, never declared by narrator. Veraine's wrongness is demonstrated by what happens when she acts on her theology, not by authorial tell. The Weave's holding is vindicated through plot outcomes, not through stated affirmation. Reader's experience of the book's Force metaphysics is emergent from events — the argument arrives as felt conclusion, not as position-taking. No character gives a summative speech reconciling Weave-rendering with light/dark canonical framing; the reconciliation happens in the reader's head, unforced.

derived_rules.name: Ben's diagnostic-voice discipline (R11)
derived_rules.content: Ben's close-third register tracks what he has earned. Analytical precision arrives as experience accrues. Parts 1-2 render his perception as first-approximation reading — reactive, tactile, what his body does before his mind catches up; the thing he notices and cannot name; the sentence he starts and cuts off. Sharpening arrives at Ch 13 midpoint and Ch 21 SPP. Ben does not analyse like Sera; he observes, and his observations refine over the book's length. Drafting pipeline must not import late-Ben analytical register into early-Ben scenes. If a Part-1 sentence of Ben's interiority could be lifted into a mission debrief, it is too composed for the scene.

derived_rules.name: Jacen parallel subtextual after Ch 18 (R13)
derived_rules.content: The Jacen parallel is named explicitly once (Ch 18, second pinch point) and thereafter operates subtextually. Ch 19-28 do not re-articulate the parallel in dialogue or narration. Reader holds it as accumulated reading, refreshed by events rather than statements. Ch 21 s2 (Torin walks, group does not seal) and Ch 28 s2 (Luke's 'you didn't call me') carry the parallel most heavily — both land without naming it. Also applies to touchpoint 5 (Ch 25-26 if any) and touchpoint 6 (Ch 28 s2).

derived_rules.name: Torin rendered through Ben (D7)
derived_rules.content: Narrator does not over-signal Torin's direction past Ben's perception. Torin is rendered only as Ben sees him, and Ben's reading is wrong in specific ways we can feel. This is the Trauma Lie (D1) under test in the middle chapters. Single-POV discipline includes refusing to give the reader access to Torin's trajectory that Ben does not himself have. Some readers will run ahead of Ben, some behind — feature, not bug.

derived_rules.name: Kael self-driven beats rendered unexplained (W1)
derived_rules.content: Kael's self-driven plants and inversions (Ch 7 archive request, Ch 8 observation to Desh, Ch 15 approach to Torin, Ch 17 direct question) each live briefly and unexplained. Ben's close-third registers and moves on — no 'Kael had been acting differently lately' narration, no Ben-POV interpretation of the beat's meaning. Reader holds each beat as character-texture rather than plot-signal.

derived_rules.name: Veraine's ledger voice (W2)
derived_rules.content: Veraine's ledger entries and archive annotations are precise and certain without affect. No taunts, no editorial commentary on her opponents, no breaks in register, no performance of triumph or contempt. The working mind is the character — what she notices, how she frames it, what she does not think worth writing down. Minimal adjectives. Intellectual restlessness expressed as what-else-might-follow-from-this, never as doubt.

derived_rules.name: Climax comm-channel discipline (B3)
derived_rules.content: In Ch 25-26, Force-sense carries atmospheric presence of the containment-node infrastructure; comm-channel carries only tactical-language-required information (Desh's decisions, timing calls, responses to queries). No running narration over comms. The heartbeat beat — node wobble in Weave-sense, Desh's re-stabilisation comm — alternates channels for suspense, not as exposition template. Desh is not felt directly through the Force; only the nodes are.

derived_rules.name: In-character Weave variants (D3)
derived_rules.content: Characters use in-character variants of 'the Weave' per terminology_registry.in_character_variants — Maetha-era voice 'cloth', Torin/Sera 'stitching', Veraine/Ankhural 'threadwork', Gavran-archive 'work'. Only the narrator uses 'the Weave' consistently as the canonical referent. Ben inherits the narrator register in his close-third but may shift register when quoting or internally echoing another character's voice.

line_level_rules: Never use 'a sense of' or 'a feeling of' — describe the sensation directly
Never use 'couldn't help but' — characters make choices, they don't succumb to narrative inevitability
Never use 'it was as if' more than once per chapter — prefer direct metaphor or simile (and note: the Force does not have 'as if'; it has 'is' or 'is not')
Never use 'he realized' or 'she realized' as a revelation delivery mechanism — show the realization through reaction and changed behavior
Never use 'little did he know' or any omniscient narrator intrusion — we are locked in close third
Never use 'suddenly' — if something is sudden, the sentence structure should convey that through pacing, not adverb
Never use 'indescribable' or 'beyond words' — if the narrative says something can't be described, the narrative has failed
Never describe a character's eyes changing color or glowing to indicate emotion (except established Force effects)
Avoid 'felt a chill run down his spine' and all variants — find original physical responses to fear/dread
Avoid starting paragraphs with 'And then' — this is a pacing crutch
Avoid 'the young Jedi' or 'the Skywalker heir' as Ben substitutions — use 'Ben' or 'he', never epithets
Avoid 'ancient wisdom' or 'timeless knowledge' when describing archive content — be specific about what the knowledge IS
Avoid adverb-dialogue-tag combinations ('he said quietly', 'she whispered softly') — let the dialogue and context convey tone
Limit exclamation points to actual exclamations — never in narration, rarely in dialogue
Never use 'reach out with the Force' more than twice in the entire manuscript — find varied descriptions for Force-perception
Never write 'the particular quality of X', 'the specific kind of Y', or 'a certain quality of Z' — these are AI-typical literary hedges that delay the actual observation

Never use 'the way X does Y' or 'the way X did Y' as a simile construction ('comfortable the way old furniture is comfortable', 'the way a door that doesn't latch is wrong'). This is a literary-fiction tic. Prefer direct description or a clean simile with 'like' — but still sparingly
No more than ONE simile per paragraph. Do not develop a simile across multiple sentences or paragraphs. Pick the image and move on
Do not describe one sensation with multiple stacked metaphors in the same scene. If the wrongness is a missing note, it is not also a seam, a missing tooth, and a gap. One metaphor, used consistently
No more than 2 consecutive paragraphs of pure internal monologue before dialogue, action, or concrete external observation. Interiority is salt, not the dish
Keep paragraphs short. Aim for 2-3 sentences average. A six-sentence introspective paragraph is a warning sign — break it up with dialogue, action, or environment
Open scenes with action, dialogue, or concrete observation — not with an atmospheric multi-clause sentence or mood-setting simile
Prefer short sentences. When in doubt, cut the subordinate clause. Ornate syntax is not the voice of this book (except inside a permitted Stover beat)
Do not use sentence fragments as a literary stylistic tic. A fragment for emphasis once or twice per scene is fine; a pattern of fragments is wrong for this register

Dialogue should carry more of the scene than interior monologue. If a scene is 70% inside Ben's head and 30% exterior, rebalance toward dialogue and action (Bujold-interior register does not mean extended interior monologue; it means warmth calibration inside brief interior beats)

anti_patterns: No prophecy fulfillment structure — the story is about choices, not destiny. No character should feel 'fated' to do anything.
No dark side temptation scenes where a character hears whispered voices or sees visions of power. The technique's danger is more subtle and more interesting than standard dark-side temptation.
No training montages — Ben is already a competent Knight. The survivors don't need to learn modern techniques. Growth happens through experience and relationship, not practice sessions.

No 'chosen one' framing — Ben's unique Force perception (the wrongness) is a plot mechanism, not a destiny marker. Other Skywalkers could potentially perceive it too; Ben is simply in the right place and state of mind.
No villainous monologues — Veraine presents arguments, not speeches. She never explains her plan because she doesn't need to justify herself to opponents.
No redemption-through-combat — no character switches sides because they're defeated in a lightsaber duel. Ideological change comes through evidence and experience, not physical submission.
No 'the Force wills it' as explanation — the Force in this story is a system with properties, not a sentient guide. Characters may believe the Force guides them, but the narrative never confirms it.
No convenient timing — if two events coincide, establish the causal or thematic connection. Coincidence is the enemy of earned narrative.
Avoid the 'wise mentor explains things' pattern — Sera, Torin, and Kael are knowledge sources but they should disagree and be wrong about things. No single character has all the answers.
Avoid resolution through superior firepower — the climax is won through collaboration and trust, not through being stronger. The Weave-resonance is not a superweapon.
voice_definition.force_description_guidelines: The Force in this story has specific phenomenological rules defined in the force_mechanics.sensory_vocabulary section. Key principles: (1) The Weave (normal Force) is perceived as textured, directional, with distinguishable aspects — like a handrail in the dark, always where expected. (2) The unwoven Force (the wound) is perceived as formless, directionless — the handrail is gone but the wall is still there, somewhere. Abilities function without the feedback loop. 'Losing color vision' — everything present but meaning drained. (3) The technique's activation is perceived as active structural violence — a pulling, a suction, the Weave leaning toward the practitioner and coming apart thread by thread. Like standing next to a drain. (4) Weave-resonance is perceived as unprecedented — three textures interacting, producing an overtone none could create alone. Starts discordant, catches when the practitioner stops trying to lead. Warmth returning after cold. A chord building from notes that shouldn't harmonize but do. (5) Desh's non-Force-sensitive experience escalates from environmental unease through physical wrongness (chrono drift, temperature shifts, wrong vegetation) to grief-without-an-object at full unweaving — validating that the Weave matters to everyone, not just Force-users. Character-differentiated sensations: Ben perceives unweaving as a missing handrail (the concept-vs-sensation rule: body-experience first, analysis second); Sera perceives it as the architecture going slack; Torin perceives it as relief; Kael perceives it as the old familiar (his Sith training fits the unwoven state better than the Weave); Desh perceives it as chrono-drift and wrong-growing vegetation and, at full unweaving, grief without object.
voice_definition.pacing_feel: Zahn-clear surface pacing — propulsive, sentence-level clarity, dialogue and action carrying momentum — with Luceno payload density sitting underneath the surface in what each scene is *about*. Early chapters exploratory and haunted; middle chapters increasingly compressed by institutional discovery and character pressure; Parts 3-4 tighten into urgent forward motion without losing sequel beats for moral consequence. Ch 13 midpoint and Ch 21 SPP spike into Stover-interior register; Ch 25-26 climax extends that allowance. Ch 27 earns the book's most visible humor and quietest interpersonal warmth (Bujold-forward). Most chapters land between 3,250 and 4,250 words, with structural spikes at Ch 5, 13, 21, 25, and 26. Pacing anti-pattern: if a chapter is moving slowly because the sentences are slow, rewrite the sentences; if it is moving slowly because the payload is genuinely heavy (Ch 5, Ch 12), the payload is correct and the scene structure compensates through reaction-led exposition and ensemble architecture.
voice_definition.narrative_voice_notes: This is adult Legends fiction for EU-literate readers — Luceno-density payload inside Zahn-clarity prose, with Bujold-warmth interior. The target reader finished Darth Plagueis, Outbound Flight, and Memory; they are comfortable with dense political-theological payload and moral ambiguity. Interior monologue is brief and emotionally textured — Bujold-calibrated, not Stover-extended — with self-awareness and warmth supplying the register. Dialogue and action carry more of the scene's length than interiority. When Ben reflects, he reflects in one or two sentences with warmth and self-awareness, then the scene moves. Force phenomenology is experiential and sensory per the concept-vs-sensation rule — one sharp image beats a paragraph of metaphorical excavation. Ben's close-third filter is the anchor: if a sentence could not plausibly arise from his perception in real time, it does not belong on the page. Prose that the reader looks *through* to the story is the goal; prose the reader admires for its craft is the warning sign (except inside permitted Stover beats at Ch 13 / 25 / 26). This is not airport-bookstore commercial tie-in fiction; it is also not literary-fiction experimentation. It is a specific hybrid: clear sentences, dense content, warm interior.

prior_eu_onboarding.principle: The book is a Legends novel: FotJ/LotF-literate readers are the primary audience. But a reader who knows the broad Legends shape without owning every Ben/Jacen/Mara beat should never feel like they walked into the middle of a conversation. First mentions of backstory load carry invisible context — one phrase, not a paragraph.

first_mention_handling.Mara Jade: First mention earns one grounding phrase (e.g., '— his mother —' or '— before Jacen killed her —'). Do not set aside a sentence to re-explain. Do not paraphrase her death; name it and move.
first_mention_handling.Jacen Solo / Darth Caedus: On first mention, let the emotional weight do the work. A single qualifier ('his cousin', 'who had been Jacen before he was anything else') carries more than a clause of summary. Later mentions stand alone.
first_mention_handling.Galactic Alliance Guard (GAG): First mention needs two beats: that Ben served in it as a teenager, and that it is the thing he and Desh share. Never spell out the full acronym in dialogue; the characters lived it.
first_mention_handling.Vestara Khai: Referenced indirectly in Part 1 (a past a Ben avoids), more directly only if a scene requires it. If she is named, note the betrayal in one phrase — 'the second person he had let in' — and keep moving.
first_mention_handling.Abeloth: Functional on first mention: 'the Abeloth crisis', 'after Abeloth'. Does not need a character recap. Modern Jedi reference her the way real-world professionals reference a named past event.
first_mention_handling.The Vong War, Malachor, Centerpoint, Nat: Historical context only. Anchor to era ('the Vong War's scars', 'older than the Vong War') rather than explaining. A reader who does not catch the reference is not lost; a reader who does feels rewarded.

prior_eu_onboarding.anti_pattern: No onboarding paragraph. No 'as everyone knew' or 'it was common knowledge that.' No flashback sequences to summarize backstory. If a reader needs a fact to understand the present scene, deliver it through something a character notices, says, or refuses to say — never through a narrator explaining the EU to them.

lived_galaxy_texture.principle: A novel that happens only in Temple offices, ship interiors, ruins, and bunkers will feel mission-bounded — more operations report than Legends novel. Zahn, Allston, and Luceno all seed the galaxy as lived-in: cantinas, bazaars, spaceport lines, civilian traffic, local governance. The Ruusan Atonement inherits that obligation.
placement_requirements: At least one early chapter (Ch 1-4) should register Coruscant or a survey stop as a place people live in — not just a setting Ben operates inside. Even a beat of civilian foot traffic, a merchant's voice at the landing pad, or the ambient politics of the Galactic Alliance era counts.

At least one mid-book chapter (Ch 6-12) should include a stop that is not a ruin, not a breach site, and not a Jedi/Sith installation. A spaceport world, a salvager hub, a contested border sector — somewhere the crisis reads differently because the locals do not know it is happening.
Chapter 19 (the Jedi outpost) is an existing anchor for modern galactic life touched by the crisis. Treat it as the template, not the exception.

Part 4 can compress into mission spaces — that earns its own claustrophobia. But Parts 1-3 should leave the reader with a sense that the galaxy is populated, political, and going about its business while Ben and the survivors move through it.
texture_inputs: Galactic Alliance politics post-FotJ: the Alliance exists, the Senate is functional, factions argue. Mentioned in passing, not explained.
Civilian economy: shipping, agriculture, trade routes. A survey world has settlers; settlers have opinions.
Local governance: planetary moffs, sector governors, system representatives. Most do not matter to the plot; some do.
Non-human species population: the galaxy is not a human drama. Background characters are Bothans, Mon Calamari, Sullustans, Rodians, Duros, Twi'leks — not as commentary, just as population.
Ambient technology: traffic patterns, holonet feeds, street-level commerce. Established Star Wars texture, used sparingly.
lived_galaxy_texture.anti_pattern: Do not add filler scenes for texture. Let civilian and political context bleed in through the edges of existing scenes — a line of dialogue at a spaceport, a headline on a datapad, a bystander's reaction. Texture by implication, not by set-piece.

The Jedi Order operates from the Coruscant Temple under Grand Master Luke Skywalker. The Empire has been reduced to a remnant state. The Yuuzhan Vong War ended decades ago. Abeloth has been defeated but the Force is still settling.

Referencing 'the prequels', 'the original trilogy', or any film/book as a source
canon_profile.franchise_terminology_notes: The Force should be described through experiential and mystical language, not clinical or scientific framing. Avoid 'energy field' — Luke's generation understands the Force as a living presence, not a measurable phenomenon. Technology should use Star Wars vocabulary consistently: datapads not tablets, transparisteel not glass, durasteel not steel, turbolifts not elevators.

force_mechanics.primary_rule: The Force has a Weave — a woven structure that maintains the light/dark distinction and provides moral intuition to Force-sensitives. This Weave may be imposed rather than natural (per the Ankhural Codex). It can be locally unwoven by a technique derived from studying historical Force wounds (Nathema, Malachor V), creating an unwoven zone where moral intuition and Force-feedback disappear while raw ability persists. The technique removes rather than destroys — silence, not violence. It unpicks the Weave thread by thread, leaving the Force present but unstructured, like pulling the warp out of a fabric and watching the cloth come apart.
implications: Unweaving does not remove Force ability — it removes the feedback loop that tells a user whether their action aligns with light or dark. Abilities function but without moral compass.
Prolonged exposure to unwoven Force erodes emotional range and replaces identity rather than consuming it ('The caldera does not consume you. It replaces you.').
The Weave can be reinforced through harmonic resonance between disparate Force traditions working in concert — a theoretical solution never tested before the climax.
The wound amplifies emotional extremes in nearby Force-sensitives. Not possession, but pressurization — arguments hit harder, fear cuts deeper, doubt paralyzes.

The seal containing the wound was maintained by twelve Force-sensitive anchors embedded in its infrastructure as living structural components. As anchors died over centuries, the seal degraded progressively until cascading failure.

Cascade-acceleration: anchor losses do not weaken the seal additively but multiplicatively. Each failed anchor shifts load to the survivors and shortens their remaining lifespans. Veraine's escape removed an anchor that was already counter-loading the others' decay; the cascade did not begin in 47 ABY by coincidence. Ben's pressure clock is therefore not 'the seal is eroding' but 'the rate of erosion is itself accelerating.'

Veranthos sits on a natural nexus in the Weave — a place where the Force's woven structure is unusually dense and accessible. The nexus's properties explain both the Brotherhood's interest and the wound's severity.
The technique exists at different scales: personal (Caldera Knights, Torin — meters), battlefield (Gavran at Veranthos — kilometers), and the expanding wound (planetary, over centuries).

Weave-infrastructure sensing: a non-Force-sensitive trained observer (Desh) registers the Weave's failure as a pattern of correlated environmental wrongness — chrono drift, temperature inconsistencies, biological aberration, ambient affect. He cannot perceive the Weave but he can read its absence. By Ch 10 he is the most reliable instrumental indicator the group has, because the Force-users' own perception is being pressurized by the same field they are trying to measure.
force_mechanics.canon_grounding: Builds on established Legends precedents: Nathema (KOTOR/TOR — world stripped of Force by Vitiate's ritual), Malachor V (KOTOR II — wound in the Force from mass death via Mass Shadow Generator), and the concept of Force wounds as persistent phenomena. The Weave, the unweaving technique, nexus points, and anchor system are original extrapolations from these canon foundations. The Ankhural Codex and technique lineage are entirely original.

sensory_vocabulary.concept_vs_sensation_rule: The Force is rendered through body-experience first, analysis second. A scene shows the sensation (the missed footing, the missing weight, the warmth or its absence) before any character or narrator names what it means. Diagnostic vocabulary — 'unweaving,' 'the Weave,' 'amplification,' 'Weave-resonance' — is earned by experiential rendering and may not arrive on the page until the body has already arrived. The reader should feel the wrongness as Ben's body feels it; the word for the wrongness comes after.

character_differentiated_sensations.ben: The Weave registers as a handrail in the dark, the footing he doesn't think about until it isn't there. Unweaving is footing gone — not falling, but the moment before falling, when the body knows the floor has stopped agreeing to be a floor. Reaching for the Force returns presence without direction. He notices what the Force is not telling him before he can articulate what it usually does.
character_differentiated_sensations.sera: The Weave is architecture — load-bearing, structural, intelligible. She perceives it the way a Force-lock cracker perceives a sealing pattern: as a system with weight and seams. Unweaving is the architecture going slack. The walls are still walls but they no longer hold the building up. Her Force-lock expertise gives her a vocabulary the others lack and the ability to read counter-preparation in Torin's behavior at Ch 21 — she is the first to recognize that he has been engineering the SPP, not arriving at it.
character_differentiated_sensations.torin: The Weave is restraint. He has spent a thousand years being held by it. Unweaving is relief — the first quiet after a long noise. He does not register it as wrongness; he registers it as the natural state Ankhural described, which is exactly the misperception that condemns him. Ch 13 is not horror for Torin. It is recognition.
character_differentiated_sensations.kael: The Weave is the foreign accent he has been forced to learn. The unwoven Force is his first language. He moves through Ch 13 with the economy of someone who is finally home, and the wrongness he feels is at how comfortable he is — the body remembering what it was conscripted out of.
character_differentiated_sensations.desh: He cannot perceive the Weave directly. He perceives the world the Weave organizes — chrono, temperature, vegetation, animal behavior, ambient mood. As the Weave fails, those readings de-correlate and then anti-correlate. By Ch 10, his instruments and his trained eye are the group's clean instrument, because the Force-sensitives' perception is being warped by the same medium they are trying to measure. At Ch 13's full unweaving he experiences grief without an object — a sadness with no referent that does not lift until they leave the zone. The non-Force-sensitive reader meets the wound here, on Desh's body, in language that owes nothing to mysticism.

normal_weave.force_sensitive: The Force as a continuous, directional field. Reaching out provides coherent feedback — spatial awareness, emotional resonance from nearby beings, a sense of flow and direction. Light and dark distinguishable the way warm and cool are — immediate sensation, not analysis. The Force has texture: dense near living things, thin in dead space, flowing along paths with almost-gravitational logic. Reaching for the Force feels like reaching for a handrail in the dark and finding it exactly where expected.
normal_weave.non_force_sensitive: Nothing. The Weave is invisible to non-Force-sensitives in normal conditions. (For a trained observer like Desh, normal conditions are the calibration baseline against which thin-place readings register as drift.)

thin_places_mild.force_sensitive: The Force responds but the distances are wrong. Reaching for the handrail and finding it six inches further than expected — not gone, but misplaced. Spatial awareness through the Force develops a slight parallax error. Emotional resonance from nearby beings is blurred. Light and dark distinguishable but the boundary is fuzzy, like looking through frosted glass. Persistent low-grade disorientation, like the early stages of an ear infection affecting balance.
thin_places_mild.non_force_sensitive: Nothing overt. Maybe a sense that the light is wrong, or sounds carry differently. Unease without a source. (Desh, calibrated, registers chrono drift in the third decimal place — visible only against a baseline he has been keeping for hours.)

thin_places_moderate.force_sensitive: The parallax error is worse. The Force has gaps — moments where reaching gets nothing, then it's back. Intermittent rather than consistent. Dark-side residue bleeds through because the Weave that normally contains it has holes. Emotional impressions from the past leak through — not visions, not ghosts, but emotional textures without sources. A flash of cruelty that isn't his. A wave of fear from no one present. The Force is becoming unreliable as a sensory organ.
thin_places_moderate.non_force_sensitive: Temperature inconsistencies, sounds carrying oddly, a persistent sense of being watched that training identifies as environmental rather than tactical. Desh starts annotating the readings rather than just recording them — the de-correlation is now visible to the eye, not just the instrument.

thin_places_high.force_sensitive: The boundary between light and dark shifts while watched — not gone but mobile. The Weave is flexible rather than thinned. The Force responds differently depending on micro-positioning. Like a room where the acoustics change from corner to corner. A seductive quality — the flexible Weave offers freedom from the rigid light/dark binary. It feels like possibility. That seduction is part of the danger.
thin_places_high.non_force_sensitive: Chrono drift (timepiece and subjective time disagree). Light behaving subtly wrong — shadows at slightly incorrect angles. Persistent low-level headache that starts on arrival and stops on departure. Desh's readings now anti-correlate with where the Force-users say the wrongness is densest — the field is bending the perception of the perceivers, and his instruments are the only voice in the room that isn't being moved.

full_unweaving.force_sensitive: The handrail is gone. Reaching for the Force and finding something — energy, presence, potential — but no structure. No direction. No light or dark. No texture. Like trying to see in a world where light exists but nothing reflects it. The Force becomes a vast, formless pressure. Not hostile. Not empty. Undifferentiated. Every Force instinct fires into nothing. The emotional component is worst: the Force-mediated layer of moral perception goes silent. Not overridden by the dark side — absent. Navigation by judgment alone, without the safety net of Force intuition. For a Skywalker, existential.
full_unweaving.non_force_sensitive: Gravity feels subtly inconsistent. Temperature changes block to block without explanation. Chrono drifts measurably. Biological wrongness visible: wrong-growing vegetation, animals without pattern, silence where birds should be. Underneath, a persistent emotional undertone — not Force-mediated, but the biological effect of losing the ambient woven framework. Feels like grief without an object. A sadness about nothing that doesn't lift until leaving the zone. Validates that the Weave matters to everyone, not just Force-sensitives.

active_technique.force_sensitive: Different from passive breach zones. The Weave is being unpicked in real time — structural violence, not absence. A pulling, a suction — the threadwork near the practitioner leaning toward them and coming apart. Like standing next to a drain. The practitioner becomes a void in Force perception — not empty but hungry. Their Force presence transforms into something that consumes structure. The boundary of the unwoven zone is sharp — one step in the Weave, the next step nothing. A cliff edge, not a gradient.

weave_resonance.force_sensitive: Starts discordant — three notes that don't form a chord. Three traditions trying to combine approaches that have never been combined. Feels clumsy, unstable. The breakthrough comes when the practitioner stops trying to lead and listens instead. The three notes find their own relationship — not any single tradition's structure, but something emergent. Once caught: warmth. Not metaphorical — physical perception of warmth through the Force after the bone-deep cold of unweaving. The Weave reforms not as rigid grid but as living tissue — flexible, dynamic, responsive. Feels like hearing a note you didn't know you were part of. Relief, not triumph. The return of structure after its absence.
weave_resonance.non_force_sensitive: The environmental wrongness lifts. Chrono runs correctly. Temperature consistent. The grief-without-an-object dissipates. The place feels right in a way it didn't before. No mystical experience — just the absence of wrongness.

vocabulary_variation.purpose: Across a hundred-thousand-word single-POV novel, one dominant metaphor becomes a drumbeat. The Weave/handrail/frequency family defined above is the canonical conceptual model — but on the page it must be expressed through rotating sensory vocabularies so the reader never notices the same image twice in a row.
rules: The word 'Weave' is a concept term — use it sparingly (a handful of times across the manuscript) and never twice in the same scene. In-character variants ('cloth,' 'stitching,' 'work,' 'threadwork') carry the speaker's signal and should be used in dialogue per character_voices.
The 'handrail in the dark' simile is introduced once, in an early chapter, and not reused verbatim. Later echoes draw from other rotation families.
'Frequency' / 'note' / 'chord' language clusters around Force-perception scenes. Outside those scenes, prefer structural or somatic vocabulary.
Do not describe the same sensation with more than one metaphor in the same paragraph. Pick the image and move on.
When in doubt, prefer a concrete physical sensation (weight, temperature, sound, balance) over a continued metaphor.

Concept-vs-sensation: render the body-experience before naming the mechanism. Diagnostic vocabulary ('unweaving,' 'the Weave,' 'amplification array,' 'Weave-resonance') is earned by experiential rendering and may not arrive in the prose ahead of the felt sense.
forbidden_repeat_phrases: like a handrail in the dark
the note held slightly below pitch

canon_constraints.continuity: Star Wars Legends (Expanded Universe), post-Fate of the Jedi, 47 ABY
canon_constraints.divergence_point: Diverges from published Legends continuity by introducing the Ruusan Atonement thread — the Ruusan Reformations recontextualized as penance for the Jedi Lords' forbidden technique (a localized unweaving of the Force's Weave created at the Battle of Veranthos c. 1000 BBY). The seal containing that wound has been maintained by the Order for a thousand years; in 47 ABY it begins to fail.
canon_preserved: Ben Skywalker as Jedi Knight, son of Luke and Mara Jade Skywalker
Jacen Solo's fall to Darth Caedus and his murder of Mara Jade
Ben's service in the Galactic Alliance Guard (GAG) under Jacen as a teenager
The Abeloth crisis and its resolution in Fate of the Jedi
Ben's prior relationship with Vestara Khai and her choice of the dark side
Luke Skywalker as Grand Master of the Jedi Order
The Ruusan Reformations (1000 BBY) as a real historical event in the EU timeline
The Brotherhood of Darkness and Lord Kaan as pre-Reformations Sith entities
canon_overridden: The true purpose of the Ruusan Reformations: published Legends treats them as a restructuring for military and doctrinal reasons; this AU treats them as a dual-purpose event — public reform plus private penance for the Jedi Lords' forbidden technique

The existence of the forbidden technique lineage (Nathema study -> Malachor V wound fragmentary records -> Quelling of Tython -> Nihil Reach experiments -> Ankhural Codex -> Drathul IV incident -> Caldera Knights -> Gavran's technique)

Darth Veraine (Brotherhood of Darkness alchemist) and the three Jedi survivors (Sera Varik, Torin Hal, Kael Drenn) sealed as Force-sensitive anchors in the containment infrastructure since the final stage of the New Sith Wars, along with nine other anchors who died over the millennium
The Battle of Veranthos as a decisive (but previously erased) New Sith Wars engagement where Gavran deployed the technique at maximum scale
The Force's Weave as a potentially imposed structure rather than a natural property — the Ankhural Codex's heretical theoretical framework

The Brotherhood of Darkness's operation at Veranthos: an attempt to invert the Weave at a natural nexus, which would have permanently shifted the Force's structural baseline toward the dark side. Gavran deployed the technique to counter the inversion — stopped it but created the permanent wound. The tragic symmetry: inversion vs. removal, with removal proving worse because structure, even wrong structure, is better than no structure.
style_constraints: Decapitalize 'galaxy' in all contexts unless starting a sentence
Hyperdrive classifications, ship specifications, and planetary names must match Wookieepedia entries where existing canon applies
Technology and Force abilities must respect established Legends-era specifications
'Jedi' is both singular and plural — never 'Jedis'
'Darth' as a Sith title is capitalized when preceding a name; generic 'the Sith' lowercase

referenced_characters.name: Luke Skywalker
referenced_characters.role: Jedi Grand Master, Ben's father — appears in Chapters 1-2 and 28

referenced_characters.name: Jacen Solo
referenced_characters.role: Deceased — referenced in backstory, GAG parallel, thematic shadow

referenced_characters.name: Jori Teth
referenced_characters.role: Jedi Knight, Ben's sparring partner in Ch1 training salle. Background character — exists to provide the physical context of Ben's combat slip; not characterized beyond a brief interaction.

referenced_characters.name: Master Ava Renn
referenced_characters.role: Modern Jedi Knight stationed at the Outer Rim outpost (Ch19). Primary instructor at the outpost's junior training program. Her meditative practices have been failing for weeks as the seal weakens.
referenced_characters.initial_location: Outer Rim Jedi outpost (within two jumps of Veranthos)

referenced_characters.name: Knight Tell Maran
referenced_characters.role: Modern Jedi Knight at the Ch19 outpost. Newly Knighted, posted there as rotation. Has been sending increasingly urgent reports that read like stress complaints because he has no framework for Weave distortion.

referenced_characters.name: Knight Drevin Los
referenced_characters.role: Modern Jedi Knight at the Ch19 outpost. Older, senior of the three. His meditation failing has shaken him most — he built his identity around disciplined Force contemplation.

referenced_characters.name: Vess Oran

referenced_characters.name: Pira Kul

referenced_characters.name: Serran Voth
